definitions: A high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filter or ultra-low penetration air (ULPA) filter, designed to remove at least 99.97% of airborne particles 0.3 micrometers or larger in diameter.
A filter that provides the highest level of filtration efficiency, often used in critical environments like cleanrooms or hospitals.
examples: The cleanroom uses an absolute filter.
Absolute filters are crucial for sterile environments.
